comparisons.title: Analog vs analytical vs digital photogrammetry
comparisons.note: Three ways of solving the same projective problem: by mechanism, by equation, and by algorithm on digital images.

values.principle: Optical–mechanical re-creation of the taking rays; the instrument is the computer.
values.representation: Stereoscopic model in the instrument; drawn contours and planimetry.
values.input: Metric film from calibrated aerial cameras; geometry restricted by instrument design.
values.estimation: Manual orientation (Gruber points), operator measurement with floating mark.
values.evaluation: Residuals at control points; experience-based accuracy rules.
values.advantages: Robust, direct visual control; dominant production method for decades.
values.limitations: Expensive, specialised, no rigorous error propagation, limited camera types.

values.representation: Coordinates of points, camera orientations with covariance.
values.input: Film measured on comparators or analytical plotters; any camera with calibration.
values.estimation: Least-squares bundle adjustment with self-calibration and statistical testing.
values.advantages: Rigour; flexibility of geometry; quantified accuracy.
values.limitations: Measurement still manual; computing cost in early decades.

values.principle: Analytical geometry applied to digital raster images with automatic matching.
values.input: Scanned film or digital aerial cameras; GNSS/INS orientation.
values.estimation: Automatic aerial triangulation; least-squares and semi-global matching.
values.evaluation: Check-point RMSE; standardised mapping accuracy classes.
values.advantages: Automation of point transfer, DEM and orthophoto production.
values.limitations: Matching failures on low texture; designed for structured aerial blocks.

comparisons.title: Photogrammetric aerial triangulation vs Structure from Motion
comparisons.note: Largely the same mathematics, developed with different priorities.

values.principle: Bundle adjustment of a planned image block.
values.representation: Orientations, tie points, ground control in a geodetic datum.
values.input: Calibrated metric cameras, designed overlap, GNSS/INS.
values.estimation: Least squares with statistical outlier tests and self-calibration.
values.evaluation: Precision, reliability, check points against independent ground truth.

values.principle: Automatic incremental or global reconstruction from unordered images.
values.representation: Sparse points and camera poses in an arbitrary frame.
values.input: Any images, unknown or approximate calibration (EXIF).
values.estimation: Feature matching, RANSAC, minimal solvers, repeated bundle adjustment.
values.evaluation: Reprojection error, completeness, registration rate, benchmark poses.
values.advantages: Fully automatic; robust to uncontrolled capture.
values.limitations: Arbitrary scale/datum; systematic errors can go undetected without control.

comparisons.title: Multi-View Stereo vs Neural Radiance Fields
comparisons.note: Measuring surfaces versus learning a function that reproduces images.

values.principle: Photo-consistency of surface points across views.
values.representation: Depth maps, dense point cloud, mesh.
values.estimation: PatchMatch or cost-volume search; fusion; meshing.
values.evaluation: Accuracy and completeness against reference geometry.
values.limitations: Fails on specular, transparent, textureless surfaces; limited view-dependent appearance.

values.principle: Differentiable volume rendering of a learned radiance field.
values.representation: Continuous density and view-dependent colour (MLP or grids).
values.limitations: Geometry implicit and not guaranteed accurate; slow rendering; per-scene training.

comparisons.title: NeRF vs 3D Gaussian Splatting
comparisons.note: Implicit volumetric field versus explicit rasterised primitives.

values.principle: Ray marching through a continuous field.
values.representation: Neural network or feature grids queried at sample points.
values.input: Posed images; random or SfM-free initialisation.
values.advantages: Compact; smooth continuous field; strong anti-aliasing variants.
values.limitations: Many network evaluations per pixel; slow rendering.

values.principle: Tile-based differentiable rasterisation of projected Gaussians.
values.representation: Millions of explicit anisotropic Gaussians with SH colour.
values.input: Posed images plus SfM sparse point cloud for initialisation.
values.estimation: Gradient descent with adaptive densification and pruning.
values.advantages: Real-time rendering; fast training; editable explicit primitives.
values.limitations: Memory; aliasing/popping; Gaussians are not surfaces; floaters.

comparisons.title: Optimisation-based SfM vs feed-forward reconstruction
comparisons.note: Rigorous estimation per scene versus learned inference across scenes.

values.principle: Explicit geometry: matching, minimal solvers, bundle adjustment.
values.representation: Cameras and sparse points; dense MVS optional.
values.input: Images with sufficient overlap and texture.
values.evaluation: Reprojection error, pose accuracy, registration rate.
values.limitations: Slow; fails with few views, low texture, or dynamics.

values.principle: Transformer regresses pointmaps and cameras directly.
values.representation: Per-pixel pointmaps, depth, camera parameters, confidence.
values.input: One to hundreds of images; no calibration needed.
values.estimation: Single forward pass; optional BA refinement.
values.advantages: Seconds instead of minutes–hours; works with sparse views.
values.limitations: Training-data dependence; uncertainty and metric reliability still under study.

comparisons.title: Deformation-field vs native 4D Gaussians
comparisons.note: Two ways to put time into Gaussian representations.

values.principle: One canonical scene warped to each time by a learned field.
values.input: Multi-view or monocular video with poses.
values.estimation: Joint optimisation of Gaussians and deformation.
values.limitations: Struggles with appearing/disappearing content and topology change.

values.principle: Primitives defined directly in space-time (or tracked per frame).
values.representation: 4D Gaussians sliced at each t, or per-frame Gaussian trajectories.
values.estimation: Optimisation of 4D parameters or per-timestep poses.
values.evaluation: Novel view-time synthesis; tracking accuracy (trajectory methods).
values.advantages: Handles transient content; explicit temporal extent.
values.limitations: Memory scales with duration; correspondence not guaranteed (4D slices).
